claims.text: NiTi-based shape memory alloys exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation in a solution heat-treated state.
The temperature-dependent deformation is caused by thermally activated martensitic transformations.
Yield stress decreases as temperature increases.
The proposed material is equiatomic or near-equiatomic NiTi.
The solution-treated initial state contains a mixture of martensite and austenite.
Controlled heat treatment can produce a stable martensitic microstructure at lower temperatures.
Mechanical testing should span room temperature to above the austenite finish temperature.
The proposed applied stress range is below approximately 600 MPa.
The structural mediator is reversible transformation between martensite and austenite.
Elevated temperature increases the austenite phase fraction.
Elevated temperature reduces the stress required for martensitic transformation.
The change in transformation stress lowers yield stress and alters plastic flow.
Increasing temperature produces a measurable increase in plastic deformation.
The mechanical changes are tied to a progressive martensite-to-austenite transformation.
The effect is most pronounced near the martensitic transformation temperature range.
The relevant example temperature range extends from room temperature to approximately 200 degrees Celsius.
Oxidation or temperatures well above the transformation range may confound the observed response.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes a reduced stress for martensitic transformation as temperature rises, while the predicted outcome attributes the same trend to a progressive martensite-to-austenite transformation. The relationship between these oppositely directed transformation descriptions is not resolved.
